submission.justification: Radiator-R3 is the strongest available recommendation once the humidity-risk constraint is considered. The full-thickness scan showed R1 gives the largest raw pion/kaon separation near 3 cm (~4.5 sigma), but R1 is an unprotected porous radiator and the documents provide no humidity-ageing evidence for it. R2 is a solid lower-index radiator and is therefore the conservative humidity-risk option, but its simulated separation is much lower (~3.0 sigma near its optimum). R3 is the only high-separation candidate with explicit hydrophobic treatment in candidate_specs.md; around the optimum thickness it gives about 3.8 sigma at 10 GeV/c (best local repeated simulations at 3.1 cm averaged ~3.84 sigma), substantially better than R2 while addressing the moisture-risk issue better than R1. Therefore I recommend Radiator-R3 at 3.1 cm, with the caveat that the project documents supplied do not contain a numerical 10-year humidity-ageing transparency-loss result, so the hard ageing requirement cannot be independently certified from the documentation alone.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c subject to constraints
requirements.evidence: Simulation scan: R3 gives ~3.8 sigma near 3 cm; repeated local simulations at 3.1 cm gave results 4.025, 3.749, 3.913, 3.729, and 3.798 sigma, averaging ~3.84 sigma. R2 peaks around ~3.0 sigma. R1 is higher in raw separation (~4.5 sigma near 3 cm) but is not selected because it lacks documented humidity protection/evidence.

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Radiator-R1, Radiator-R2, and Radiator-R3; the recommendation selects Radiator-R3.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md identifies Radiator-R3 as a porous radiator with hydrophobic treatment, and gas_volume.md says the vessel is flushed with dry nitrogen during operation. However, none of the supplied project documents reports a numerical transparency-loss percentage after the 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test, so compliance with the ≤10% hard limit cannot be certified from the available evidence.
The recommended thickness is 3.1 cm, within the allowed 1–6 cm range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended radiator and thickness
